comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the pinned manifest SHA-256 8ea0e636bae1c90bfbf20e418fe7684f6be968d341af2d672eae305c361ee93c. Checked all 110 entries and hashes with no gaps or selector mismatches: 54 task modules, 54 matching task configs, one base config, and the dynamic task registry. Compared every task/config filename pair and read align_blocks.py, align_blocks.yml, and task_registry.py completely.
comparisons.objective: Both tasks use a separate rigid alignment tool to change the relative planar poses of multiple rigid workpieces into a common aligned geometry, followed by robot/tool withdrawal. The candidate uses a travelling bridge gauge on two rails; align_blocks uses a set square on three blocks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both centrally test contact-guided pushing/repositioning with a third-body reference tool, coupled planar alignment, and avoiding disturbance of the finished arrangement. Longer rails, tighter tolerances, bimanual execution, and six repeated checks increase difficulty but do not create a different underlying ability.
comparisons.success_condition: RoboDojo requires the three blocks to be in a straight aligned row within its configured line/orientation thresholds and the robot returned to origin. The candidate requires two rails parallel within 2 mm, six gauge seats, gauge parking, settling, and open clear grippers. Both ultimately score tool-mediated relative alignment plus withdrawal.
